observed_defect: The front timber-log face lacks a clearly defined timber frame hierarchy between the flat log courses; previous roof-edge fascia intersected the shingles and was visually rejected despite measurable geometric contact.
design_intent: Create a restrained independent post-and-lintel wooden frame on the camera-facing front facade, below roofline and away from door and stair: two narrow vertical timber uprights and one shallow horizontal top rail. Do not intersect roof tiles or staircase; preserve all source UV, mesh, access, and silhouette.
expected_visual_difference: The watchtower's uninterrupted front log wall gains two vertical dark wooden framing edges and one tidy thin horizontal cross beam tucked below the shingles. The roof should remain completely unobstructed and stairs fully visible.

actions.reason: A slender upright fastened along the outer front log wall adds intentional timber-framing order without overlapping the eave or stairs.
Weathered timber slightly darker than original for coherent depth and medieval timber joinery without repainting original atlas.
A matching right post defines a readable vertical rhythm across the log facade, deliberately below the rail and free of the stair path.
Repeat identical aged timber material for structural cohesion rather than introducing new material type.
Join the two posts with a shallow lintel set below the existing sloping roof to avoid the previous distracting roof-crossing board.
Make rail part of the same integrated medieval wood frame; preserve source material UV and roof silhouettes.
